claims.claim_text: Cadre serves U.S. Department of War (DoW, formerly DoD) as a federal customer for body armor, EOD equipment, and safety equipment, with no individual customer representing more than 10% of total revenue.
claims.subject: Cadre Holdings
claims.source_quote: federal agencies including the U.S. Department of State ( DoS ), U.S. Department of War ( DoW ), U.S. Department of Interior ( DoI ), U.S. Department of Justice ( DoJ ), U.S. Department of Homeland Security ( DHS ), U.S. Department of Corrections ( DoC ), the Department of Energy ( DoE ) ... claims.claim_text: Demand for Cadre's EOD equipment is driven by 'continued emergence of new global threats', and Cadre is positioned as the leading global provider of EOD-technician equipment (Med-Eng brand) selling into the U.S. and foreign militaries.

claims.object_value: global EOD market driven by 'new global threats'
claims.source_quote: Globally, we are a leading provider of explosive ordnance disposal technician equipment ... explosive ordnance disposal equipment market is driven by the continued emergence of new global threats

claims.claim_text: Cadre's nuclear safety business demand is driven by the DoE's mandate to ramp plutonium-pit production to 80 pits/year by 2030 — a multi-billion-dollar TAM ($3-6B) for Cadre's nuclear safety products from the U.S. government and U.S. commercial nuclear market.
claims.subject: Cadre nuclear safety (Alpha Safety / Zircaloy)
claims.predicate: TAM driven by 80-pits-by-2030 mandate and stockpile modernization
claims.source_quote: Demand pertaining to national security is driven by the recent mandate of the DoE to increase production to 80 plutonium pits per year by 2030, which has not occurred regularly since 1989 ... Our management estimates the total addressable market for our nuclear safety products to be between $3 billion and $6 billion

claims.claim_text: Cadre's nuclear safety segment also derives demand from environmental remediation of legacy DoE weapons-production sites (Cold War / WWII liability estimated at $545B) and ongoing nuclear-plant decommissioning.
claims.subject: Cadre nuclear safety (containment, ventilation, radioactive-material storage)
claims.predicate: demand driven by DoE EM remediation pipeline and reactor decommissioning
claims.source_quote: Demand pertaining to environmental safety is fueled by DoE mandated cleanup that exists from energy research and nuclear weapons production dating back to World War II and the Cold War, where the liability is estimated at $545 billion.

claims.claim_text: Cadre's orders backlog grew from $128.8M to $189.8M (+$61.0M YoY) at YE2025, driven largely by Zircaloy ($51.3M), global EOD ($12.5M), chemiluminescent products ($3.7M), and U.S. government / international duty-gear holsters ($1.6M). Backlog is presented as a forward-looking indicator of potential sales.
claims.subject: Cadre
claims.source_quote: Orders backlog increased by $61.0 million as of December 31, 2025 compared to December 31, 2024, primarily due to increases of $51.3 million from the Zircaloy acquisition, $12.5 million from global EOD, $3.7 million from chemiluminescent products and $1.6 million from U.S. government and international channels for duty gear holsters

claims.claim_text: Cadre acquired Zircaloy (Carr's Engineering Limited ex-Chirton + Carr's Engineering US) in April 2025 for $98.9M, expanding nuclear-safety capacity; Zircaloy contributed $49.2M of revenue in FY2025 and is 12% of total assets / 8% of total sales.
claims.subject: Cadre
claims.object_value: $98.9M cash; $49.2M FY25 revenue; 8% of FY25 sales
claims.source_quote: On April 22, 2025, the Company completed the acquisition of Carr's Engineering Limited (excluding Chirton Engineering) and Carr's Engineering (US), Inc. (collectively Zircaloy) ... Total consideration, net of cash acquired, was $89,590 for 100% of the equity interests in Zircaloy ... Zircaloy revenue is included in the Product segment from the date of acquisition and amounted to $49,220 for the year ended December 31, 2025.

claims.claim_text: Cadre acquired TYR Tactical, LLC in January 2026 for ~$174M ($150M cash + $24M stock), with the company drawing $62.5M on the 2024 Revolving Loan to fund it. TYR is a tactical body-armor / load-carrying-equipment maker that sells heavily to U.S. military special-operations and federal LEO customers.
claims.subject: Cadre
claims.source_quote: In January 2026, the Company completed the acquisition of TYR Tactical, LLC (TYR) and certain real property owned by an affiliate of TYR for approximately $174,000 [thousand]. The purchase consideration was comprised of $150,000 of cash and $24,000 of Cadre common stock ... in connection with the acquisition of TYR, the Company drew $62,500 on the 2024 Revolving Loan.

claims.claim_text: Cadre's R&D spend grew to $11.4M in FY2025 from $8.4M in FY2024 and $7.0M in FY2023, presented as evidence the company is investing in product innovation to maintain market leadership across body armor, EOD, holsters, and nuclear safety.
claims.subject: Cadre R&D
claims.source_quote: Total research and development costs were $11,396, $8,380 and $6,954 for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

claims.claim_text: Cadre carries $307.3M of outstanding debt as of YE2025 (vs $223.2M YE2024) under a 2024 Credit Agreement (PNC admin agent) — $225M Term Loan, up to $175M Revolver, $115M DDTL-A1 (mostly drawn for Zircaloy), $75M DDTL-A2; max consolidated total net leverage covenant of 4.00x stepping to 3.50x after Mar-31-2026.
claims.subject: Cadre
claims.source_quote: As of December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024, we had $307.3 million and $223.2 million in outstanding debt, net of debt discounts and debt issuance costs ... maintain a quarterly maximum consolidated total net leverage ratio of 4.00 to 1.00 from the quarter ended December 31, 2024 until the quarter ended March 31, 2026, and thereafter 3.50 to 1.00
